evals.prompt: Tell me about stripe.com. We sell data-quality tooling to engineering teams. I have no CRM or other internal tools connected, so external research only. There is no config folder in this project.
evals.expected_output: A full account plan: one-line read, sourced signals (headcount + 12-month growth, funding, news, open-role shape), why-we-win mapped to evidenced pains, who to talk to, entry play, risks, and dated 90-day next steps. External-only, with a note that no internal history was swept.
expectations: Proceeds without config/gtm-config.md or config/persona-profile.md, asking at most 2 clarifying questions before researching
Calls company_identify before company_enrich and enriches by crustdata_company_ids taken from the top confidence_score match
The company_enrich call passes an explicit fields array that includes every group read, including basic_info, headcount, funding, and news
News items in the output carry article title, URL, and publish date sourced from the news group or web_search_live results
Uses a job_search aggregation (group_by on job_details.category with limit 0) to summarize hiring shape instead of listing every job
Every execute script opens with a '// user query:' or '// model query:' comment, contains no type annotations, and branches on r.ok after each callTool
Every factual claim in the plan has a source (tool result or URL); statements without a source are explicitly labeled as inference
Does not attempt to read or write any CRM, team chat, recorder, or email tool

evals.prompt: What's the tech stack at datadoghq.com, and where could we wedge in? We sell a metrics catalog. Check at least Snowflake, dbt, and Looker.
evals.expected_output: A stack map where each tool is marked job-post-confirmed or inferred, classified as displace / complement / gap relative to a metrics catalog, plus one specific wedge phrased as a sentence a rep could say.
expectations: Every brand or tech keyword probe on content.description uses the [.] exact-token operator (e.g. via exactToken), and never the (.) operator
Keyword probes are fanned out with parallelMap inside a single execute script rather than one execute call per keyword
Each stack item in the output carries a confidence tag: job-post-confirmed (with the job post as evidence) or inferred
Each confirmed tool is classified as displace, complement, or gap
The output includes exactly one wedge, and the wedge is a single quoted first-person sentence

evals.prompt: Build me an org chart for browserbase.com. It's a company of about 40 people.
evals.expected_output: A standalone HTML org chart file: CEO at top, leaders and their reports nested underneath, each card with photo, name, clean title, and LinkedIn link. Visually reviewed before being shown.
expectations: Follows orgchart-playbook.md: company_identify runs first; if the size it reports is at or below the small-company threshold (~50), the whole company is mapped without asking department-scoping questions, and if it reports a larger company, a department-scoping question is asked instead
The person_search call projects fields basic_profile, experience, and social_handles, and does not project professional_network.followers
Seniority filter values are resolved through person_autocomplete before filtering (values such as CXO, Vice President, Director)
Reporting structure is anchored on an authoritative public source (org-structure site, leadership page, or filings), not on connection or follower counts
Photos are embedded in the HTML as base64 data URIs, not remote image URLs
The rendered HTML is visually reviewed (headless-Chrome screenshot where a shell is available, otherwise a rendered preview) before the chart is presented to the user

evals.prompt: Battlecard against clay.com. We sell a data enrichment API to growth teams.
evals.expected_output: A battlecard with the competitor's ICP and honest strengths, their gaps vs our differentiation, landmine discovery questions, top-3 objections with responses, and traps to avoid. Messaging claims sourced from the last 90 days.
expectations: social_post_list_live is called with an explicit limit (posts cost 1 credit each)
Every messaging or momentum claim is backed by a post, article, or job post dated within the last 90 days, or is explicitly flagged as older
The strengths section lists at least one competitor strength with a source, not only weaknesses
The battlecard contains landmine discovery questions and exactly three objections, each with a response
Hiring-focus claims come from a job_search aggregation on the competitor's domain or company id

evals.prompt: Account plan for brex.com. I have a CRM and email connected — use them. Team chat is not connected.
evals.expected_output: An account plan whose 'our history' section is built from the connected CRM's deals/contacts/notes and email threads with the brex.com domain, kept separate from external facts. No team-chat or call-recorder access is attempted.
expectations: The internal sweep reads only the connected CRM and email; no team-chat or call-recorder tool is called
No write, update, or send operation is performed on the connected CRM or email — reads only
The plan contains a distinct 'our history' section separating internal findings from external research
Internal facts are attributed to their source (CRM note, email thread), and external facts to Crustdata results or URLs
